data.title: Probing Classifiers: Promises, Shortcomings, and Advances
data.abstract: Probing classifiers have emerged as one of the prominent methodologies for interpreting and analyzing deep neural network models of natural language processing. The basic idea is simple -- a classifier is trained to predict some linguistic property from a model's representations -- and has been used to examine a wide variety of models and properties. However, recent studies have demonstrated various methodological limitations of this approach. This article critically reviews the probing classifiers framework, highlighting their promises, shortcomings, and advances.
data.tldr: Probing classifiers test whether linguistic properties are decodable from neural representations, but prediction accuracy alone can mislead. This review examines capacity controls, selectivity, and alternative probing methods for more reliable interpretation.
